# opnsense_dnsmasq_boot (Resource)

Dnsmasq network boot entries (Services > Dnsmasq DNS & DHCP > DHCP boot): the PXE/TFTP boot file and server handed to DHCP clients.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "opnsense_dnsmasq_tag" "pxe" {
  tag = "pxe"
}

# Hand clients tagged "pxe" the iPXE loader from the TFTP server.
resource "opnsense_dnsmasq_boot" "ipxe" {
  filename       = "ipxe.efi"
  server_address = "192.168.10.5"
  tags           = [opnsense_dnsmasq_tag.pxe.id]
  description    = "iPXE"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `filename` (String) Boot file, e.g. `pxelinux.0` or `ipxe.efi`.

### Optional

- `description` (String) You may enter a description here for your reference (not parsed). Defaults to `""`.
- `interface` (String) This adds a single interface as tag so this DHCP boot option can match the interface of a DHCP range. Empty matches any interface. Defaults to `""`.
- `server_address` (String) Boot (TFTP) server address; empty uses this firewall. Defaults to `""`.
- `server_name` (String) Boot server host name. Defaults to `""`.
- `tags` (Set of String) If the optional tags are given then this option is only sent when all the tags are matched. Can be optionally combined with an interface tag. UUIDs of `opnsense_dnsmasq_tag` resources; empty applies to all clients. Defaults to `[]`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) UUID of the entry.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by UUID
terraform import opnsense_dnsmasq_boot.example 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
